newsitem.title: PERU: Peru govt says ready to resume talks with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Peru govt says ready to resume talks with rebels.

text.p: Peru government negotiator Domingo Palermo said Friday he was ready to resume talks with Marxist rebels holding 73 hostages in Lima but ruled out acceptance of their main demand, freedom for 400 of their jailed colleagues.

Palermo told a news conference arrangements had been made for him to meet the rebel leader in a building near the besieged residence of the Japanese ambassador where the hostages are held and Canada's ambassador would act as a witness. He did not say when the meeting would take place.

Although Palermo presented the meeting as definite, it was not clear if the rebels had agreed to it. They broke off a previously-planned face-to-face meeting with Palermo over the government's refusal to discuss their main demand.
"As is publicly known, the Peruvian state is not going to release the MRTA prisoners," Palermo said.
But he added: "I am ready to start the conversations...the meeting will be held in a building close to the residence."
He said a Red Cross vehicle would transport Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebel leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini to the site of the meeting.
